With a market cap. of around $103 billion, Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) is a global travel platform that connects travelers with unique accommodations, experiences, and services offered by local hosts. With over 5.5 million hosts and more than 2.5 billion guest arrivals across almost every country, the company helps people explore destinations and connect with local communities in authentic ways.

The San Francisco, California-based company is set to announce its fiscal Q3 2026 results after the market closes on Thursday, Nov. 5. Ahead of this event, analysts expect ABNB to report a profit of $2.89 per share, up 30.8% from $2.21 per share in the year-ago quarter. The company has surpassed Wall Street's earnings estimates in one of the last four quarters while missing on three other occasions.

For fiscal 2026, analysts forecast the vacation home rental company to post an EPS of $5.29, an increase of 31.3% from $4.03 in fiscal 2025.

Shares of Airbnb have surged 34.6% over the past 52 weeks, outpacing both the S&P 500 Index's ($SPX) 13.1% gain and the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF's (XLY) 4.1% decline over the period.

www.barchart.com

Airbnb shares climbed 17.4% following its Q2 2026 results on Aug. 6 after revenue beat estimates, rising 16.5% year over year to $3.61 billion and topping analysts' forecast, and EPS increased to $1.37. Global nights and seats booked rose 10% to 148.3 million, supported by strong worldwide travel demand, a boost from first-time users during the FIFA World Cup, and high-single-digit booking growth in North America - the strongest regional growth in almost three years.

The company also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to at least mid-teens growth, up from its previous low-to-mid-teens forecast, while hotel-night bookings grew nearly three times faster than home bookings, reinforcing optimism about its expansion beyond vacation rentals.

Analysts' consensus view on ABNB stock is cautiously optimistic, with a "Moderate Buy" rating overall. Among 40 analysts covering the stock, 20 recommend "Strong Buy," four suggest "Moderate Buy," 14 indicate "Hold," one gives "Moderate Sell," and one advises "Strong Sell." This configuration is more bullish than three months ago, with 18 analysts suggesting a "Strong Buy."

title: Airbnb vs. Chewy: Do Pets or Places Power One Stock More than the Other?
detail:
Airbnb vs. Chewy: Do Pets or Places Power One Stock More than the Other?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 24, 2026 at 1:40 PM EDT 7 min read
ABNB
CHWY
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As global travel habits evolve and pet ownership remains a staple of household spending, investors are frequently comparing Airbnb Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) and Chewy Inc. (NYSE:CHWY) to find the best growth opportunities.

Airbnb acts as a dominant platform for alternative accommodations and experiences, whereas Chewy serves as a dedicated digital ecosystem for pet products and healthcare. Both companies rely on consumer discretionary spending but face vastly different competitive landscapes and regulatory environments.

The case for Airbnb

Airbnb operates a peer-to-peer marketplace that connects over 5 million hosts with guests seeking unique travel experiences. The company does not own the properties on its platform, which allows it to scale quickly as more hosts join the travel and tourism stocks ecosystem. It focuses on integrating artificial intelligence to personalize search results and has developed partnerships with major cultural and sports organizations to keep its brand relevant.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $12.3 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 11% compared to the previous year. The company reported a net income of roughly $2.5 billion for the period. While net income remained strong, its net margin, which shows how much of each dollar of revenue becomes profit, came in at about 20.4%, down slightly from the previous fiscal year.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Airbnb maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.3x. This ratio compares a company's total debt to its shareholder equity, with lower numbers generally indicating less financial risk. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets, was close to 1.4x. Free cash flow reached about $4.6 billion, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 34% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since stock-based compensation is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Chewy

Chewy serves as a leading e-commerce destination for pet owners in the United States and Canada, offering roughly 190,000 different products. Its strategy centers on the Autoship subscription program, which provides predictable revenue and high customer loyalty. Recently, the company has expanded its reach into pet health through Chewy Pharmacy and Chewy Vet Care clinics, including the strategic acquisition of Modern Animal.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $12.6 billion, which was an increase of about 6.2% over the prior year. The company generated a net income of around $222.8 million. Its net margin was approximately 1.8%, reflecting the competitive nature of retail, where high volumes are often balanced by narrower profit figures per sale.

Growth investors focus on stocks that are seeing above-average financial growth, as this feature helps these securities garner the market's attention and deliver solid returns. But finding a growth stock that can live up to its true potential can be a tough task.

In addition to volatility, these stocks carry above-average risk by their very nature. Also, one could end up losing from a stock whose growth story is actually over or nearing its end.

However, the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects, makes it pretty easy to find cutting-edge growth stocks.

Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) is on the list of such stocks currently recommended by our proprietary system. In addition to a favorable Growth Score, it carries a top Zacks Rank.

Studies have shown that stocks with the best growth features consistently outperform the market. And for stocks that have a combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), returns are even better.

While there are numerous reasons why the stock of this company is a great growth pick right now, we have highlighted three of the most important factors below:

Earnings Growth

Earnings growth is arguably the most important factor, as stocks exhibiting exceptionally surging profit levels tend to attract the attention of most investors. For growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is highly preferable, as it is often perceived as an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.

While the historical EPS growth rate for Airbnb is 22.8%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 31.2% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 28.3%.

Impressive Asset Utilization Ratio

Asset utilization ratio -- also known as sales-to-total-assets (S/TA) ratio -- is often overlooked by investors, but it is an important indicator in growth investing. This metric shows how efficiently a firm is utilizing its assets to generate sales.

Right now, Airbnb has an S/TA ratio of 0.52, which means that the company gets $0.52 in sales for each dollar in assets. Comparing this to the industry average of 0.51, it can be said that the company is more efficient.

While the level of efficiency in generating sales matters a lot, so does the sales growth of a company. And Airbnb is well positioned from a sales growth perspective too. The company's sales are expected to grow 15.8% this year versus the industry average of 3.2%.

What Needs To Be True To Buy Airbnb Stock Now?

Anyone looking at Airbnb (ABNB) stock right now faces a main worry: the shares returned 36.7% over the past twelve months, compared with 15.1% for the S&P 500, so a new buyer may be arriving late. Still, the business behind the stock accelerated in 2026. Revenue rose 16.5% in fiscal Q2 2026, up from 12.7% growth in the same quarter a year earlier. So what does a buyer pay for that growth today?

Airbnb Stock Costs Far More Than The S&P 500

Airbnb stock trades at 38.7 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 23.0 for the S&P 500. Buyers get faster growth for that price. Over the past three years, Airbnb's revenue grew 13.2% a year on average, compared with 5.9% for the S&P 500.

That gap in growth appears to be what a buyer is paying for. The premium lasts only as long as Airbnb keeps growing faster than the companies in the index, and the company pays no dividend to fall back on while you wait.

Can Airbnb Keep Growing This Fast?

Management expects reported growth to hold through the September quarter, though currency does part of the work. On its August 6, 2026 call, management guided revenue growth of 15% to 17% for fiscal Q3 2026. The company also raised its full-year outlook to at least mid-teens growth, up from low-to-mid-teens. About three percentage points of the third-quarter growth comes from currency, management said, so the pace from the business itself is lower than the guided range.

Airbnb's newer hotel push could add to that growth. Hotel nights are growing about three times faster than the homes business, management said, though hotels are still a single-digit percentage of nights booked.

The risk specific to Airbnb comes from Europe. European cities will gain more leeway to curb short-term rentals like those on Airbnb under new EU plans, news reports said on September 9, 2026. On its August call, management said policy is a risk but not an existential one, and a risk the company will manage forever.

How Far Has Airbnb Stock Fallen In Past Selloffs?

Airbnb stock fell further than the S&P 500 in each of the last five market shocks. In the 2022 inflation shock, it fell 48%, compared with 24% for the S&P 500. In the 2025 US tariff shock, it fell 33%, compared with 19% for the index. A buyer paying a premium is taking on a stock that has fallen close to twice as far as the market when markets turn.

For a buyer at today's price, several factors need to hold: revenue growth near management's outlook, more nights from hotels, and little lost to the new EU plans. Airbnb is expected to report its fiscal Q3 2026 results in November 2026. Its revenue growth against the 15% to 17% guide is the number to watch.

Investors choosing between Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) and DoorDash (NASDAQ:DASH) must weigh global travel dominance against the rapid expansion of local delivery services as both companies mature into profitable enterprises.

Airbnb connects travelers with unique stays and experiences worldwide, while DoorDash facilitates the delivery of food, groceries, and retail goods. Although they operate in different industries, both rely on massive network effects and are prominent names among consumer discretionary stocks today.

The case for Airbnb

Airbnb operates a global marketplace for stays and travel experiences, serving hosts and guests in more than 220 countries and regions. The company generates a significant portion of its business from outside the United States, with approximately 61% of revenue coming from international listings in its latest annual report. Its strategy focuses on expanding the number of high-quality hosts and improving the user experience for travelers, often competing with established travel sites such as Booking Holdings and Expedia Group.

On a trailing-12-month (TTM) basis through Q2 2026, revenue reached $13.1 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of approximately 13%. The company reported net income of nearly $2.7 billion for the period, resulting in a net margin of roughly 20%. This high level of profitability demonstrates the company's ability to generate significant earnings from its travel marketplace operations even as it continues to invest in new international markets.

As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.3x, meaning it holds $0.30 in total debt for every dollar of shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.4x, indicating the company has $1.40 in short-term assets for every $1 of liabilities due within one year.

Trailing free cash flow was nearly $4.9 billion. However, you should note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 34.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because it is a non-cash expense.

The case for DoorDash

DoorDash provides a local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery workers, known as Dashers. By the end of 2025, the platform supported over 56 million monthly active users and partnered with more than 600,000 merchants. Its business strategy involves expanding beyond restaurant delivery into groceries and retail, while growing its subscription services, such as DashPass, to build customer loyalty in a competitive on-demand market.
